texts: Strange is the road: the traveler who stands still reaches the goal, and the runner remains where he began.
doha w a traveler: paradox, the one not moving gets there first
traveler, upside-down saying
Give me a doha in the upside-down style of the old sants about a traveler who walks all his life without arriving, while the one who sits still in the heart has reached the destination long ago.
A traveler friend of mine journeyed through forty countries and came back more lost, while his stay-at-home aunt seems to have arrived somewhere; that irony deserves a riddle-doha.
The brow is marked and the heart is bare; the plain brow hides a heart marked with grace.
The man with the elaborate forehead mark is the one I trust least, and the man with nothing on his brow the most; it is a funny reversal.
forehead mark, reversed
doha w a forehead mark, paradox style, holy looking ppl are unholy
I'd like a doha in the style of riddling reversals about a forehead mark that makes a man look pure while his heart is stained, and another with a bare forehead whose heart is bright.
doha with a palanquin, riddle style, the carried one is poorer than the carriers
In the palanquin the rider is the weary one, and the bearers carry a lightness he has never known.
At a wedding the groom in the palanquin looked more worn than the men carrying him, singing; it struck me as upside-down.
Write an upside-down doha about a palanquin where the one who is carried is heavy with worry and the one who carries it sings freely, showing that things are the reverse of what they seem.
palanquin, topsy-turvy
My uncle says the richest man he knows owns nothing and the poorest has everything, and I want that paradox captured in a doha.
Write a doha full of riddling reversals: the poor man is a king, the king is poor, the silent one speaks loudest, and the seeing are lost, in the upside-down way the old saints liked.
He who owns nothing owns the world; he who owns the world is owned by it.
upside-down sayings
doha w a paradox in it pls, kabir style riddle
The mother is born of her child, the teacher taught by his pupil: such is the topsy-turvy way.
I have noticed that my toddler teaches me more about patience than anything I ever studied, a reversal worth a riddle-doha.
Craft a doha in the manner of the saints' inverted sayings, where the student teaches the teacher, the child begets the parent, and the one who loses everything is the only one who wins.
doha w a paradox, the opposite of what u expect
world turned upside down
salt, inverted riddle
doha w salt, riddle style, the thing that vanishes is what you taste
Write an upside-down doha about salt that disappears into the dish and yet is the only thing the taste remembers, so that what vanishes becomes what remains, and absence is the greatest presence.
I added salt to my cooking and it vanished, yet the whole dish changed; I find that riddle strange and beautiful.
The salt is gone, yet all is salt; the one who vanished became the whole.
The door is open yet no one enters, the jaggery sweet yet bitter to the taste: all is topsy-turvy here.
Please make a doha in the riddling style about a door that is wide open yet nobody can walk through, and jaggery that tastes bitter to the greedy, showing the world turned upside down.
door, jaggery, paradox
doha w door + jaggery riddle, nothing is as it seems
Everyone tells me the door is open, but nobody walks through, and the sweetest jaggery turns bitter in a greedy mouth; a riddle-doha for that please.
A wise old man told me the more he gives away, the more he has, and the more I hoard, the poorer I get; I want a doha that captures the paradox.
doha on giving away makes u richer, kabir paradox style
Write a doha in the saints' riddling manner where the empty is full, the full is empty, the giver is rich, the hoarder poor, and everything stands reversed from what the world believes.
empty is full
What is given grows; what is hoarded withers: so the world turns upside down.
I need a doha in riddles about a man who marks his forehead and stands at the door of holiness, yet is farthest from it, while the unmarked one who never knocked is already inside.
The man at the door of the shrine with the biggest forehead mark was the least kind, and the quiet fellow with a bare forehead was already inside the spirit of it; that reversal fascinates me.
door, forehead mark, reversal
doha w door + forehead mark, the ones outside are inside
The marked brow waits at the door; the bare brow is already within: how strangely the world turns.

Can you put together a doha in the upside-down style about the slow tortoise who arrives first while the swift one is left behind, the stillness that travels farther than speed, and the world that rewards the reverse.
My grandfather walked at a tortoise's pace and always finished before the rest of us who rushed; that irony deserves a riddling doha.
The tortoise sleeps and arrives, the swift runs and is lost: strange are the ways of the world.
doha w tortoise, paradox, slow wins
tortoise, topsy-turvy
The rope binds the one who holds it, and frees the one who lets go: so the world stands on its head.
doha w rope riddle: u hold it tight n it holds u
The tighter I held the rope of my plans, the more they bound me, and the day I let go I was free; a paradox for a doha.
Write an inverted-sayings doha about a rope which binds him who holds it and frees him who drops it, so that the holder is the prisoner and the one who lets go is the master.
rope, reversed
doha w seed riddle: the plant is inside the seed, the seed inside the plant
The seed is born of the plant and the plant of the seed; who is the mother and who the child?
seed, riddle
Write a doha in the old riddling style where the seed holds the vast plant and the plant holds the tiny seed, and no one can say which came first, the small containing the great.
I planted a seed and was amazed that all of a huge plant lay hidden in it; it feels like a riddle with no answer.
doha with a lion paradox, the lion afraid of a lamb or smth
lion, upside-down
The lion trembles before the lamb, the lamb walks proudly past: how the world stands on its head!
My fearless uncle, a lion in business, goes meek before his tiny granddaughter, and she commands him like a ruler; that reversal belongs in a riddle.
Give me a doha in the topsy-turvy manner of the old saints about the lion who runs away from the lamb, the strong afraid of the weak, and the powerful ruled by the humble.

I'd like a doha in the manner of the old saints' upside-down sayings, where the sleeper is awake, the waker asleep, the speaker dumb, the dumb eloquent, and no one can tell which way the world really turns.
doha w paradoxes, kabir style, plz
The silent one speaks loudest, the loud speaker says nothing: such is the strange speech of the wise.
My friend says the louder people shout the less they say, and the quiet ones say everything; I would like a riddle-doha out of that.
reversals and riddles
A teacher of mine used to say that the more you understand, the less you can explain, and the less you know, the louder you speak; paradox doha?
paradox, topsy-turvy
Write a doha full of inversions: the fool is certain and the wise doubt, the dying live and the living die, and the whole world is a puzzle whose answer is the opposite of what it seems.
The more you know, the less you say; the less you know, the more you shout.
doha: weird opposite world riddle, kabir style
moth, paradox
doha w moth riddle: the moth loves the light that kills it

Craft a doha in riddles about the moth that dies in the very brightness it adores, so that love becomes its destruction and its destruction becomes its fulfillment, the reverse of how things should be.
The moth dies in the glow it loves; the dying is the living, the end the beginning.
My friend burned out chasing the passion he loved most, and he says it was worth it; this seems an upside-down thing to want, like a moth.
Please make a doha in the riddling style where the goal is farthest from the one who strives and nearest the one who rests, and the journey ends where it began, for the world is full of reversals.
I worked frantically for a goal that never came, and only when I gave up did it arrive; this feels like a riddle.
doha on the opposite of what u expect happening
The seeker never finds, the resting find; so the world turns inside out.
reversals everywhere
The pot of water floats in water: inside is water, outside is water; who then is inside whom?
Write a doha in the riddling manner about a pot of water placed in a pond: water within, water without, and the pot breaks and the two become one, so the inside and outside are the same.
doha w pot of water riddle: the water inside n outside r the same
pot of water, riddle
When I submerged an empty pot of water in a pond I noticed water inside and outside, and wondered which is which; I want a riddling doha on that.
philosopher's stone, swan, paradox
The swan perches on the philosopher's stone and starves for a grain; the wealth seeks the swan: how strange the world!
I found my sister's calm, swan-like and unaware, sitting on a fortune like a swan on a philosopher's stone, hungry; that reversal wants a riddle-doha.
doha w philosopher's stone n swan, riddle: rich but starving

I need a doha in inverted style about a swan that sits upon the philosopher's stone yet starves for a grain, the owner of the greatest wealth dying of poverty, the reverse of what anyone would expect.
Whoever dies before death lives, whoever lives before dying is dead: so runs the riddle of the saints.
die to live
After a breakdown I felt reborn, as though I had to die in order to live, and that reversal seems like an old riddle.
Can you put together a doha in the upside-down tradition where the dying live, the living die, the poor are rich, the rich are poor, and nobody can tell which way is up in the world of riddles.
doha: the more u lose the more u win, riddle style
bitter gourd, oil press, reversal
A bitter gourd that my aunt crushed in the oil press made the sweetest oil, which is a reversal I would like to see in a riddle-doha.
doha w bitter gourd + oil press riddle: bitter becomes sweet when crushed
Crushed in the oil press, the bitter gourd yields sweetness: how topsy-turvy the world!
Write a doha in riddles about a bitter gourd that gives sweet oil when crushed in the oil press, so that the bitter becomes sweet under pressure, in the upside-down way of the saints.
I stepped on a thorn in the sand and the pain taught me more comfort than a soft bed ever did; a paradox for a doha.

Give me a doha in inverted style about sand that gives a spring when pressed and a thorn that heals the one it pricks, where pain becomes comfort and the barren becomes plenty, the reverse of the world's expectation.
doha w sand + thorn riddle: pain that heals
The sand yields the spring, the thorn draws the thorn; how strangely the world is made.
sand, thorn, paradox
doha w traveler n ocean paradox: the thirsty traveler beside an ocean
I'd like a doha in the upside-down manner about a traveler dying of thirst beside the ocean, the ocean full yet empty to him, so that abundance is poverty, a reversal the saints loved to sing.
traveler, ocean, thirsty
I traveled to the biggest ocean in the world and felt thirstier than ever; I would like a riddle-doha on that odd reversal.
The traveler thirsts beside the ocean, and the ocean thirsts for a drop: such is the riddle of the world.
crow, upside-down
My neighbor's crow somehow sounds sweet while the singer in the next lane sounds harsh; I would like a riddle-doha for this reversal.
doha w crow, riddle: the crow sings sweet and the singer croaks
Write a doha in upside-down style about the crow that sings with sweet notes while the sweet singer croaks, where the ugly turns beautiful and the beautiful turns ugly, in a world stood on its head.
The crow sings sweet, the singer croaks: how strange this world, turned all around.
doha w thief + cage riddle: the thief is free, the guard is caged
The thief walks free in the open, the guard sits in the cage of his duty: whose is the prison?
A thief I read about felt freer than the rich man whose cage of fear he stole from, and the reversal kept me thinking; doha?
thief, cage, reversal
Craft a doha in the old riddling style where the thief goes free and the owner sits in a cage of worry, so the robber is rich in freedom and the rich are poor in peace.
inverted truths

Please make a doha composed of riddling reversals where the silent speak, the deaf hear, the wise play the fool, and the fool seems wise, so that all appearances stand upside down in the saints' fashion.
doha w kabir-style upside down saying
My grandmother laughed that the wise play the fool and the fool plays the sage, and I wanted to put that riddle into a doha.
The wise play the fool; the fool plays the sage; and who can tell the one from the other?

Write a doha in the manner of paradoxical sayings where the cold burns, the hot freezes, the free are bound and the bound are free, so that the world seems a riddle whose every answer is the opposite.
world reversed
doha w paradox plz, like kabir ulatbansi
My mentor says freedom is found by choosing limits, and I find it a delicious contradiction worth making into a doha.
In binding oneself, one is freed; in seeking freedom, one is bound.
doha w cloth sheet riddle: the cloth is woven by what it covers
I need a doha in riddles where the cloth sheet is woven by the one who wears it and the wearer is worn by it, until no one can say which covers which, a topsy-turvy tangle of the world.
I wrapped myself in a cloth sheet and, oddly, felt that it was wrapping me; I would like a riddle-doha for this contrary feeling.
The cloth sheet covers the sleeper, yet the sleeper covers the cloth: who then is hidden?
cloth sheet, reversal
An old man in my village says a person is strongest when he bends and weakest when he stands stiff; paradoxes like his belong in a doha.
He who bends stands tall; he who stands stiff is broken by the lightest breath.

Can you put together a doha in the saints' riddling manner where strength is found in yielding and weakness in resisting, and the wise one wins by losing, to leave the world's ordinary logic turned on its head.
weak is strong
doha on paradox, the weak win and the strong lose
empty yet full
A sage once told me that the silence in a room is louder than its noise, and I want that paradox in a doha.
doha: silence is the loudest sound, riddle kabir style
Write a doha in the upside-down tradition where the quiet speaks loudest, the still moves fastest, and the unseen is the most visible, to show how the world's ways are the reverse of its appearance.
Where words end, the song begins; where all is still, the world moves on.
yogi, moth, reversal
Give me a doha in the upside-down manner about a yogi who sits motionless yet travels farthest, and a moth that flutters ceaselessly yet goes nowhere, the still being swift and the swift being still.
doha w yogi + moth riddle: still guy goes farther than the fluttering one
The yogi sits and arrives; the moth flies and burns: still is the swift, swift the still.
A yogi I know sits still all day yet seems to have gone further than any of us restless moths; I want a riddle-doha.
doha w sandalwood + rainbird paradox: cool sandalwood burns, thirsty bird has plenty
The sandalwood cools everyone but is itself cut and rubbed, while the rainbird cries thirst in a downpour; it is an odd reversal I would like in a riddle-doha.

I'd like a doha in the riddling manner of the saints about the sandalwood that gives coolness to those who cut it and the rainbird that thirsts amid plenty, the giver wounded and the filled left empty.
sandalwood, rainbird, paradox
The sandalwood cools the hand that cuts it; the rainbird cries thirst in the flood: strange is the world.
The mark is on the brow, the arrow in the heart; the one who bears the mark is wounded, and the unmarked heals.
Write a doha in inverted riddles about a forehead mark that shines while the arrow of greed hides in the heart, so the one who looks holy is wounded and the plain one is whole.
The man with the proud forehead mark was pierced by greed like an arrow, while the plain man next to him was peaceful; it seems a backward world to me.
doha w forehead mark + arrow, riddle: the marked ones are the wounded
forehead mark, arrow, reversal
upside-down world
doha like ulatbansi, opposites everywhere
What is near seems far, what is far lies near: strange is the compass of the heart.
Whatever I chased ran away, and whatever I left behind came running after me; it feels like an upside-down law of life.
Craft a doha in the topsy-turvy sayings of the old poets, where the nearest thing is the hardest to find and the farthest is hidden in the heart, so that all the world's directions are reversed.

Please make a doha in riddles where the sword is raised in the name of peace and the mosque built on quarrel stands empty, so that the faithful are faithless and the faithless faithful, the world turned upside down.
doha w mosque + sword riddle: ppl fight for peace lol
Men were fighting with swords outside a mosque over who loved peace more, and the contradiction felt like a riddle for a doha.
mosque, sword, paradox
They draw the sword to guard the mosque of peace: how strange the guarding of calm!

Write a doha full of the saints' inversions in which the teacher learns, the student teaches, the lost one is found, the finder lost, and the world as it appears is the opposite of the world as it is.
The seeker is the sought, the finder the found: the riddle ends where it began.
After years of searching I realized the thing I looked for was looking at me, and that paradox deserves a doha.
seeker is sought
doha riddle: the hunter becomes the hunted
My aunt's churn keeps turning, yet it is the butter that moves the churn in the end; I love that odd inversion and want it as a doha.
I need a doha in the riddling tradition about a churn that churns the churner, where what is turned turns the one who turns it, and doer and deed are one, the reverse of what we expect.
I churn the churn, the churn churns me; who is the maker and who the made?
churn, riddle
doha w churn, paradox: churner gets churned
A man I know has worn out his prayer beads in the temple, but his heart has never moved, while another who never counted any is full of devotion; a reversal worth a doha.
doha w prayer beads + temple riddle: the counter is empty, the non-counter is full
The prayer beads turn in the temple, the heart stands still; the one who counts nothing is full to the brim.

Can you put together a doha in the upside-down fashion about prayer beads worn thin in the temple by one whose heart is empty, while the man who never touched a bead is filled to overflowing with devotion.
prayer beads, temple, paradox
ash, rainbird, reversal
doha w ash + rainbird riddle: rainbird wets the ash n it gives life
Write a doha in the manner of old riddles about ash from which life rises and a rainbird that finds its drink in drought, where the dead gives birth and the dry gives drink, the world turned over.
After a village disaster, from the ash a green shoot came up, and the rainbird sang in the drought; the reversal moved me.
From the ash, life; from drought, a song for the rainbird: such is the strange turning of things.
My father says the poorest days of our lives were the richest and the richest days were the poorest, a reversal I want in a doha.
Give me a doha in the saints' riddling manner, full of contradictions, in which loss is gain, gain is loss, day is night, night is day, and every certainty stands on its head.
all things reversed
Loss is the hidden gain, and gain the hidden loss: so turns the topsy-turvy wheel.
doha w nonsense-sounding paradoxes, kabir style
I'd like a doha in the upside-down way about the moth that finds life in the very glow that burns it, so that death is its birth and the end its beginning, as contrary as the world can be.
doha w moth riddle, the burning is the living
moth, contradiction
My friend threw himself into a risky love like a moth and says he has never felt so alive; a riddle-doha please.
The moth burns and is born, the glow slays and gives life: topsy-turvy is the world.
In the market the buyer is sold and the seller is bought; the whole world stands upside down.
doha w market riddle: the buyer gets bought
Write a doha in riddling reversals about a market where the buyer is the one being sold, the seller is bought by his goods, and everyone thinks they trade while they are traded, the world inverted.
In our market I saw a man buying so much that his possessions ended up owning him; there is a riddle in that.
market, topsy-turvy
river, riddle
The river runs to its end and the end flows in the river; whose is the source?
Standing by the river I wondered whether the river carries me or I carry it; an upside-down thought for a doha.
doha w river paradox: the river is thirsty
Craft a doha in the upside-down tradition about a river that thirsts though it is all flowing water, a river that runs toward what is already inside it, the ceaseless seeking of the already found.

Please make a doha in the style of the old topsy-turvy sayings about a palanquin where the passenger is the prisoner and the bearer is free, so that rank turns into bondage and humble labor into liberty.
At a village fair I watched a rich man in a palanquin look miserable while the bearers laughed, and I want a riddle-doha about that.
doha w palanquin riddle: bearers happier than the rider
The one who rides is shackled, the one who bears is free: topsy-turvy rank.
palanquin, reversal
A heron stood in white and still, yet cruel, while a small bee, buzzing and busy, did only good; I find such contrast an odd reversal for a riddle-doha.
Write a doha in riddles about the heron, calm and white, hiding cruelty, and the bee, noisy and small, bringing sweetness, so that the quiet one harms and the humming one heals.
doha w heron + bee: calm one bad, busy one good
The white heron stands in stillness and kills; the humming bee gives honey: the world turned upside down.
heron, bee, paradox
pls doha w paradoxes in the old style
Please write a doha in the old upside-down tradition where the beginning is the end, the end the beginning, the part contains the whole and the whole is in the part, to make one dizzy in thought.
It is funny that my grandfather called himself the youngest in the family, even at ninety, and the children the oldest in wisdom; a riddle for a doha.
The oldest is the youngest, the youngest the oldest of all: the circle swallows its own start.
beginning is end
He who seeks to live dies, and he who is ready to die lives: so runs the riddle of the world.
My neighbor stopped fearing and began to live fully; another feared everything and barely lived at all. A reversal like that deserves a riddle.
I need a doha in the saints' upside-down manner where the fearful die every day and the fearless live forever, where seeking life loses it and giving it up gains it, to unsettle the sleeping mind.
life and death reversed
doha w paradox about life n death
doha w physician riddle: the doctor is sick n the patient is healthy
Our local physician is sicker than most of his patients, and many of them healthier than he; that irony would make a good riddle-doha.

Can you put together a doha in the upside-down style about the physician who cures all but is himself diseased, while the patient who seems ill carries a healthy spirit, where cure and sickness trade places.
physician, paradox
The physician is sick, the sick are whole: who then shall heal the healer?
Write a doha in riddling style about a bridge that stands still while the whole world crosses it, yet the standing one is farthest traveled, and those who cross are the ones who never move.
bridge, riddle
Every day I cross a bridge that never moves, and I wonder whether I am the one traveling or the bridge; a riddle-doha please.
doha w bridge paradox: the bridge goes everywhere w/o moving
The bridge stays still and all the world crosses; who traveled, the one who stood or the ones who ran?
Give me a doha in inverted riddles where the cuckoo hides its young in another's nest, the strangers raise it, and the foster mother is the real mother, so the false is true and the true false.
cuckoo, topsy-turvy
The cuckoo's young are raised by a stranger, and the stranger is the mother: such is the riddle of kinship.
doha w cuckoo riddle: the foster mom is the real mom
My cousin raised a child who wasn't his own, and his foster love is stronger than blood, like a cuckoo's young cared for by strangers; that reversal needs a doha.
